Calling for a Hero.text: Calling for a hero means calling the police: civilians dial 110 for crimes and villains or 119 for fires and medical emergencies, and the dispatcher alerts the heroes on patrol nearby. Agencies listen to police dispatch and share the area's calls, and whichever pro is closest answers. In a busy city center a hero can arrive within minutes; in towns without a local agency the wait can be long, and police and firefighters handle the first minutes alone. Big incidents bring several agencies at once, and the first pro on scene reports to the police commander and calls for reinforcement when needed. Many agencies run public tip lines for non-urgent reports, but an emergency always goes to 110 or 119 first. Calling a specific hero by name does not work: dispatch sends whoever can arrive fastest. Prank calls and false villain reports are crimes, and the police track them down.
